name: Identity Protection Anomalous Sign-Ins
description: Microsoft Entra ID Protection scores sign-ins and directory changes that look automated, impossible, or hopped across tenants. A high-severity anomaly means Microsoft already thinks the session or the user is risky: leaked password, unfamiliar properties, or browser hopping between companies. It is not a proof by itself, but it is a strong starting point for incident response. Privileged users with high-severity Identity Protection alerts should be contained first and explained second.
mitigations: Rotate credentials if the actor is compromised
